part12_analysis_answers.q1_does_acquisition_failure_reproduce_to: In the P-C0R pilot window (14:40-15:21 UTC), NO: all 30 repeated requests and 20 A/B requests succeeded (50/50 total). Earlier today (~13:17 UTC), YES (0/9 succeeded). Thus, failure did not reproduce during P-C0R, reflecting an open access window.
part12_analysis_answers.q2_does_behavior_vary_with_time_under_fi: Across today's full session history, YES (0/9 failure at 13:17 UTC flipped to 10/10 success at 13:59 UTC with no code change). Within P-C0R's 40-minute window, NO (stable success at T+0, T+20, and T+40).
part12_analysis_answers.q3_does_client_configuration_affect_outc: NO. In 10/10 paired comparisons with alternating execution order, Arm A (discovery client with cookies and headers) and Arm B (fetch client with User-Agent only) both succeeded identically.
part12_analysis_answers.q4_what_is_the_first_failing_layer: In P-C0R: NONE (all layers L0 through L6 succeeded). In earlier failure window (~13:17 UTC): L0 (DNS resolution failure) and L1 (TCP connection reset / 45s connect timeout).
part12_analysis_answers.q5_what_exact_http_transport_behavior_oc: In P-C0R: clean HTTP/1.1 200 OK from AkamaiNetStorage/AkamaiGHost edge, complete byte streams matching Content-Length header, valid ZIP/PDF magic bytes, zero corruption, valid qpdf checks.
part12_analysis_answers.q6_does_failure_disappear_without_changi: YES. The failure observed at 13:17 UTC completely vanished by 13:59 UTC and remained absent throughout P-C0R without modifying a single line of production code.
part12_analysis_answers.q7_is_current_behavior_consistent_with_t: YES. The sharp sub-hour transition from 0/9 to 10/10 success on identical endpoints under identical network conditions is classic time-varying CDN/endpoint access behavior.
part12_analysis_answers.q8_is_there_evidence_that_the_same_mecha: NO DIRECT EVIDENCE. Historical invocation records, error logs, and HTTP telemetry are completely absent for all 318 losses. While the ~4.5-minute clustering of historical successes is consistent with time-varying availability, it does not prove historical cause.
part12_analysis_answers.q9_what_remains_unknowable_because_histo: Whether cmd_fetch was ever run against the 318 failed pairs; what error (403, 429, 503, timeout, reset) was encountered if run; how many retry attempts occurred; and whether the code used on 2026-09-11 was byte-identical to HEAD 0fb8cbf.

part13_root_cause_classification.primary_mechanism: NO_REPRODUCIBLE_FAILURE (within controlled P-C0R pilot window) / CURRENT_TRANSIENT_ACCESS_BEHAVIOR (across full multi-session observation span on 2026-09-17)
contributing_factors: OBSERVABILITY_PROBLEM: Insufficient structured persistence of fetch failures in fetch_one() / cmd_fetch, causing historical failure reasons to be lost.
CONTROL_FLOW_GAP: Silent fallthrough on exhausted HTTP 403/429/503 in fetch_one() returning None without setting last_err or logging.
ruled_out_hypotheses: CLIENT_CONFIGURATION_EFFECT: Ruled out by Part 6 paired A/B comparison (10/10 pairs succeeded under both Arm A and Arm B).
FILE_FORMAT_PROBLEM: Ruled out (100% valid magic bytes, valid ZIP and PDF archives).
VALIDATION_PROBLEM: Ruled out (qpdf validates all downloaded archives).
CONTROL_FLOW_PROBLEM: Ruled out (cohort_fetch_manifest.jsonl was a post-hoc evaluation export, not a pre-fetch filter).
